p3g2.instruction: Complete the table below. Choose NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from Reading Passage 3 for each answer.
p3g2.body: Time, Traveller, Destination, and Purpose of Travel table. Classical Greece, Herodotus, Egypt and Anatolia: Purpose 'To gather information for the study of [[29]]'. Han Dynasty, Zhang Qian, Central Asia: Purpose 'To seek [[30]]'. Roman Empire, Ptolemy, Strabo and Pliny the Elder, the Mediterranean: Purpose 'To acquire [[31]]'. Post-classical era (about 500 to 1500 CE), Muslims, from East Africa to Indonesia and Mecca: Purpose 'For trading and [[32]]'. 5th-9th centuries CE, Chinese Buddhists, [[33]]: Purpose 'To collect Buddhist texts and for spiritual enlightenment'. Early modern era (about 1500 to 1800 CE), European explorers, the New World: Purpose 'To satisfy public curiosity for the New World'. During 19th century, Colonial administrators, Asia and Africa: Purpose 'To provide information for the [[34]] they set up'. By mid-century of the 1800s, Sun Yat-sen and Fukuzawa Yukichi, Europe and the United States: Purpose 'To study the [[35]] of their societies'. 20th century, People from [[36]] countries, Mass tourism: Purpose 'For entertainment and pleasure'.
